findings.title: Converting cyclic Markdown drawing payloads can terminate the host process
findings.summary: An attacker-supplied Markdown image with a `drawing:` payload can encode a dependency pointing back to itself. `markdown_to_docx` accepts the flat JSON graph and recursively materializes it without cycle detection, exhausting the stack or memory before conversion returns.

severity.rationale: A compact input deterministically reaches unbounded recursion in a public conversion API. Impact is availability of the processing host; shared-service exposure depends on the caller deployment.
severity.changeConditions: Process isolation and strict CPU/memory budgets constrain impact; an exposed shared conversion service increases operational impact.

confidence.rationale: Direct static trace shows accepted input, unchecked dependency indexes and unconditional recursive re-entry; no deployment or runtime reproduction is assumed.

codeEvidence.label: Flat payload graph is deserialized without graph validation
codeEvidence.explanation: The attacker controls the base64 JSON and its flat dependency indexes; the JSON nesting limit does not validate graph cycles.

codeEvidence.label: Accepted drawing traverses its dependency indexes
codeEvidence.explanation: Any valid in-range dependency is passed to dep_part, including an attacker-defined self-referential node.

codeEvidence.label: Part expansion recurses before recording a completed node
codeEvidence.explanation: used tracks output names, not visited dependency indexes. A self edge repeatedly re-enters the same dependency; package deduplication occurs only after recursion returns.

rootCause.summary: Markdown image destinations are decoded into `Drawing` objects and stored by `picture()`. `package::assemble` routes them through `PartRelate::drawing()` to `materialize()`. The dependency graph is attacker-defined flat JSON; `dep_part()` bounds only each index and uses a name set for collision avoidance. It has neither an active-index set nor a traversal budget, so an in-range self edge or mutual cycle never returns.

findings.remediation: Validate drawing dependency graphs before materialization. Reject cycles and excessive traversal depth/work, and memoize materialized indexes so shared dependencies are not repeatedly expanded.

counterEvidence: Bounds checks reject out-of-range dependency indexes, but do not reject valid cyclic indexes.
check_box_regions returns success for empty boxes and does not inspect dependency graphs (drawing.rs:1569-1576).
Output-name collision handling and post-recursion byte deduplication cannot stop recursion.
limitations: No application code or vulnerability-triggering input was executed.
validation.summary: Confirmed public `markdown_to_docx` -> `read` -> `picture` -> `package::assemble` -> `PartRelate::drawing` -> `materialize` -> `dep_part`. A drawing with simple valid XML, no boxes, a root relation to dependency 0 and dependency 0 referring to itself bypasses box checks and repeatedly enters the same function.

dataflow.summary: Markdown image destination -> base64 decode -> serde Drawing graph -> document.drawings -> assembly -> materialize -> recursive dep_part cycle
dataflow.sink: unbounded native call stack and intermediate names/XML allocations

impact.rationale: Denial of service in the processing process; no read/write escape or code execution established.

likelihood.rationale: Flat small cyclic graph passes local type and index checks.

reachability.summary: Reachable through public Rust markdown_to_docx and its Python/WASM wrappers; CLI creation also forwards text to it. Requires the victim to process attacker-provided Markdown, with no control over victim configuration required.

attackPath.summary: Supply Markdown containing an image whose drawing payload has an in-range cyclic dependency, then have the host convert it with the public Markdown-to-DOCX API.

remediationTests: Assert self cycles and two-node cycles return structured errors without recursion.
Assert deeply nested and exponentially shared acyclic graphs obey an explicit work budget.
Preserve valid shared dependency round trips.

findings.title: Rendering a DOCX with a large table span can exhaust host memory
findings.summary: A short `gridSpan`, `gridBefore`, or `gridAfter` value is parsed as an unrestricted column count. The renderer expands that numeric value into per-column vectors, so a small, shallow DOCX passing admission can request gigabytes of memory.

severity.rationale: A compact attacker-controlled DOCX reliably reaches excessive allocations in normal conversion. Impact is processing-host availability; an internet-facing service is not assumed.
severity.changeConditions: Isolating each conversion and enforcing address-space and CPU limits reduces shared-host impact.

confidence.rationale: Parent verified attribute parsing, raw-row propagation, occupancy calculation and direct vector allocations.

codeEvidence.label: Cell span has no upper bound
codeEvidence.explanation: The XML attribute is converted to a machine-sized integer; max(1) only imposes a lower bound.

codeEvidence.label: Row grid skips also become unbounded spans
codeEvidence.explanation: gridBefore/gridAfter values feed placeholder cell spans and the same table occupancy calculation.

codeEvidence.label: Occupancy directly sizes vectors
codeEvidence.explanation: Summing attacker-controlled spans determines the number of f32 columns, followed by additional per-column state.

rootCause.summary: `table_block()` takes `cell_span()` results for actual cells and `row_grid_skip()` results for skipped columns, then computes the maximum sum of spans across rows. There is no column-count or allocation budget before `vec![each; occupancy]` and `cols.resize(...)`. A single span of 1073741824 requests at least 4 GiB for the first f32 vector alone, despite a short XML attribute.

findings.remediation: Validate table spans and grid skips against a documented column/work budget before addition or allocation. Use checked arithmetic, bounded aggregate occupancy, and fallible allocation with a structured refusal.

counterEvidence: Admission caps archive bytes, inflated bytes, XML depth and tag sizes, not numeric expansion; the small shallow attribute fits those limits.
Word-validity checking is separate from the conversion entry point.
Caller process limits constrain damage but do not reject this input in the library.
validation.summary: Confirmed with_layout admits original package bytes, parses main WML and reaches table_block; cell_span values propagate unchanged through RawCell (13466,13530-13535) to occupancy vectors. Normalization is namespace rewriting and imposes no numeric column limits.

dataflow.summary: DOCX XML attribute -> usize span -> RawCell.colspan -> summed occupancy -> repeated vector allocation
dataflow.outcome: memory exhaustion, allocator abort or conversion denial of service

likelihood.rationale: No optional setting; direct machine-sized numeric amplification.

reachability.summary: Public docx_to_pdf/render/PNG APIs call with_layout; CLI, Python and WASM conversion wrappers expose the same engine. Victim must process attacker-provided DOCX.

attackPath.summary: Have a victim render a DOCX whose one-cell table declares an enormous gridSpan or grid skip.

remediationTests: Reject excessive gridSpan, gridBefore and gridAfter in public render paths.
Reject aggregate overflow and excessive combined spans.
Verify ordinary merged tables retain layout.

baselineFinding.title: Unbounded DOCX table spans control allocation sizes
baselineFinding.attacker: An attacker supplying a DOCX for PDF or PNG rendering.
baselineFinding.violated_invariant: Short numeric attributes must not authorize memory allocations unrelated to the admitted input size.
baselineFinding.source_to_sink: cell_span parses w:gridSpan directly into usize with only a minimum of one. row_grid_skip similarly accepts unrestricted gridBefore/gridAfter values. table_block sums these spans into occupancy and sizes its column vector from that value. resolve_table_merges subsequently sizes another vector from the same spans.
baselineFinding.impact: A tiny table containing gridSpan=1000000000 requests billions of columns and multi-gigabyte allocations, exhausting memory or terminating the host. Larger values can also trigger capacity or arithmetic failures.
counterevidence: Package admission checks XML depth, tag width, attributes, and inflated bytes.
The triggering value is a short legal integer, so those checks do not constrain the derived allocation.
No maximum table-column count or allocation budget is applied in these paths.
Caller process memory limits remain a containment measure.
baselineFinding.remediation: Apply a documented table-column budget to gridSpan, gridBefore, gridAfter, row totals, and merge indexing. Use checked addition and refuse oversized dimensions before constructing vectors.

candidate.originalMessage: admission scans XML only by .xml/.rels suffix (except main part), while converter resolves arbitrary stylesheet target then recursively calls unchecked parse_xdocument; a deep styles.bin bypasses max_xml_depth and can overflow stack.

originalFinding.title: Auxiliary XML parts with non-XML extensions bypass admission depth limits
originalFinding.rule: Validate every XML part before recursive DOM construction
originalFinding.attacker: An attacker supplying a DOCX to a conversion application, CLI, Python binding, WASM binding, or MCP renderer.
originalFinding.violated_invariant: Untrusted package XML must obey the active InputLimits before DOM construction.
originalFinding.source_to_sink: Admission selects XML using only .xml/.rels suffixes, with a separate exception for the main document. A styles relationship may instead target word/styles.bin. The converter resolves that relationship without requiring an XML extension and passes its contents to the unchecked, recursive parse_xdocument parser. Deeply nested styles.bin content therefore bypasses max_xml_depth and reaches unbounded recursive parsing.
originalFinding.impact: A small compressed DOCX can exhaust the native stack and terminate the process or trap the WASM instance.
counterevidence: Admission bounds compressed and inflated bytes and checks ordinary .xml/.rels parts.
The main document receives an explicit extension-independent depth check.
Markdown's separate XML parser enforces policy when parsing a selected part.
These controls do not check arbitrarily named auxiliary XML before this converter path.
SECURITY.md requires caller process limits; those can contain impact but do not restore the bypassed XML policy.
originalFinding.remediation: Discover XML parts through content types and relationships, or validate each XML string immediately before parsing using the active limits. Ensure auxiliary parts receive the same depth, attribute, namespace, and tag checks as the main document.

candidate.originalMessage: altChunk HTML colspan parses unbounded usize and end_table iterates 0..sum(spans), so a tiny chunk with colspan=1000000000 generates billions of grid columns before rendering.

originalFinding.title: HTML altChunk colspan causes uncontrolled output expansion
originalFinding.rule: Bound HTML table spans before generating WordprocessingML
originalFinding.attacker: An attacker supplying a DOCX containing an HTML or MHT altChunk for rendering.
originalFinding.violated_invariant: Conversion of admitted embedded content must have bounded generated dimensions and output size.
originalFinding.source_to_sink: The renderer expands w:altChunk content before parsing the document. The HTML builder accepts colspan as an unrestricted usize. end_table sums cell spans and writes one w:gridCol element for every resulting column without checking an output budget.
originalFinding.impact:
An embedded fragment such as
x
generates a billion grid-column elements, exhausting memory and CPU before layout.
counterevidence: The archive and embedded HTML bytes are bounded by admission.
The amplification depends on a short numeric value rather than large embedded content.
Generated WML is not checked against a column or generated-byte budget before this loop.
This is a separate pre-layout expansion path from the direct DOCX gridSpan allocation.
originalFinding.remediation: Reject oversized HTML colspan values and row totals, use checked arithmetic, and enforce a generated-WML byte budget during altChunk conversion.

candidate.baseline: Chicago numbering format repeats symbol n/4 times at src/convert/mod.rs:6015-6018 with unbounded u32 list start/section page counters, allowing multi-GB allocation from a short attribute.

originalFinding.title: Chicago numbering expands a short counter into gigabyte-sized labels
originalFinding.attacker: An attacker supplying a DOCX containing controlled list or page-number metadata.
originalFinding.violated_invariant: Number formatting must have bounded work and output size for every accepted numeric value.
originalFinding.source_to_sink: parse_num_level accepts list start values as unrestricted u32. The Chicago formatter repeats one of four symbols approximately n/4 times. A level using numFmt=chicago, lvlText=%1, and start=4294967295 therefore requests 1,073,741,824 copies of a three-byte symbol. Page numbering also accepts an unrestricted u32 start and supports Chicago formatting.
originalFinding.impact: One short numbering definition can request roughly three GiB for a single label, with further copies during replacement and rendering, causing memory exhaustion or process termination.
source_evidence: let start = first_named(dom, lvl, "start").and_then(|n| dom.attribute(n, &W::val())).and_then(|s| s.parse().ok()).unwrap_or(1);
counterevidence: Other numbering formats have bounded representations or explicit normalization, including the Roman formatter.
Chicago formatting applies no corresponding limit.
XML and ZIP admission budgets do not constrain this derived string size.
originalFinding.remediation: Enforce a maximum generated label length before repetition, returning a typed resource refusal or a documented bounded fallback. Apply the same policy to list, endnote, and page-number formatting.

candidate.originalMessage: num_pr parses paragraph ilvl as unrestricted u32 (src/convert/mod.rs:12711-12714); Numbering::resolve_ilvl scans every integer down from ilvl until a defined parent (5529-5532). One normal level-0 numbering definition plus ilvl=2147483647 entails ~2.1 billion HashMap probes before rendering. If huge level is itself defined, next_marker materializes counters for all lower levels (5610-5627).

originalFinding.title: Attacker-controlled list levels trigger billions of empty lookups
originalFinding.rule: Do not enumerate numeric ranges to resolve sparse numbering levels
originalFinding.attacker: An attacker supplying a DOCX containing a numbered paragraph.
originalFinding.violated_invariant: Resolving a list level must be bounded by the number of defined levels, not an arbitrary numeric attribute.
originalFinding.source_to_sink: num_pr accepts w:ilvl as any u32. When the requested level is absent, Numbering::resolve_ilvl searches every preceding integer in reverse until it finds a defined level. A paragraph requesting ilvl=4294967295 against an abstract list defining only level zero therefore causes approximately 4.3 billion hash lookups.
originalFinding.impact: A small document can monopolize a rendering worker for a prolonged period. Repeated paragraphs or repeated requests amplify the denial of service.
counterevidence: Normal Word numbering uses very few levels.
The parser does not restrict incoming levels to that range.
Input byte and XML depth limits do not bound the numeric search.
Caller CPU limits can contain a worker but do not prevent this amplification.
originalFinding.remediation: Validate the supported numbering-level range and find the maximum defined key below the requested level by iterating existing keys. Audit ensure_level, next_marker, and render for related numeric-range loops.
